title: Use of Invasive Water Hyacinth as Fish Aggregation Devices Complicates Fisheries Management in Tropical Aquatic Ecosystems
content:
ABSTRACT

This paper addresses an overlooked conservation issue in the Global South: how invasive species, water hyacinth (Pontederia crassipes) in this case, can become embedded in human livelihood systems, creating socio-ecological traps. It synthesises ecological, social and policy dimensions, illustrating the broader consequences of human-mediated interactions with invasive species.
